_meta.purpose: The bounds this repository's CI runs under: how long each job may take, how many times a network operation may be retried, which HTTP statuses and socket errors are retryable, which dependency-audit commands must go through a governed wrapper, and which controls must report a completion record. Prepared by Phase 1 of the CI Reliability & Failure-Prevention work.
_meta.why_this_file_exists: Every control in this repository before Phase 1 protected what a gate SAYS and none protected what it COSTS. A gate can be perfectly fail-closed and still be useless if it never runs, and on 2026-09-04 that is exactly what happened twice: `Dependency audit` spent 7m01s inside one `npm audit` against a lockfile with zero advisories, and `CI · Workflow Integrity` was CANCELLED at its ten-minute cap mid-control, silently taking four later controls with it. Neither failure was a security failure. Both were duration failures, and nothing in the repository was looking at duration.
_meta.this_is_a_bound_not_a_target: None of the timeouts below is an expectation of how long a job takes. They are the point past which a job is presumed hung. `measured_seconds` records the real observed duration so the headroom is visible and a future reader can tell a deliberate bound from a guess.
_meta.validated_by: .github/scripts/verify_ci_reliability.py, enforced inside the required `CI · Workflow Integrity` context.

job_timeout_classes._note: A job's declared timeout-minutes must be > 0 and <= its class maximum. There is no minimum band: a bound tighter than the class ceiling is always permitted, and a job that finishes faster than expected is not a governance problem. What is forbidden is an ABSENT bound, a zero or non-integer bound, or one above the ceiling, because those are the three routes back to GitHub's 360-minute default.

fast-validation.description: Linting, spec validation, secret scanning, dependency auditing, aggregators. Seconds of real work; the bound exists only to catch a hang.

application-tests.description: Language test suites with service containers. The slowest measured member is CI API quality at 9m32s.

governance-integrity.description: The required workflow-integrity job. Bounded separately because its worst case is COMPUTED from this file rather than estimated — see workflow_integrity_budget.

container-build.description: Compose build, boot, migrate, healthcheck. Image pulls and layer builds dominate and vary with registry weather.

mobile-certification.description: Flutter/Android/iOS toolchain provisioning plus analyze, test and build. Xcode and Gradle setup dominate.

release-certification.description: Tag- and dispatch-triggered release gates. Never run on a pull request, so a generous bound costs nothing routinely; it still must not be unbounded.

performance.description: k6 scenarios including the optional 2h soak profile.

jobs._note: Every job in every workflow appears here exactly once, keyed `<workflow file>:<job id>`. A job present in a workflow but absent here fails the validator, and so does the reverse — an unlisted new job is the precise way a 360-minute default gets reintroduced. `measured_seconds` is null where the job has no observed successful run in the evidence used to prepare this file; those jobs are dispatch- or tag-triggered only.

reusable_workflow_calls._note: Jobs that are a `uses:` call to another workflow carry no steps of their own and cannot declare timeout-minutes; the callee's jobs are bounded instead. Listed so the validator can tell a legitimately timeout-free job from an unbounded one.

retry._note: Applies to every governed network operation. Attempts are TOTAL attempts, not retries-after-the-first.

never_retryable._note: Retrying cannot repair any of these, so burning the budget on them delays a verdict that is already known. They fail closed on the first attempt.

verdict_protocol._note: Every governed dependency audit answers with one of exactly three verdicts, in words and in an exit code. npm and composer both exit 1 for a vulnerability AND for a dead endpoint; that ambiguity is what made the 2026-09-04 incident take six minutes of log archaeology, and separating the two is the whole point.
verdict_protocol.why_that_ordering: A run that saw a 503, retried, and then found real advisories prints both the outage banner and the finding. Matching the outage patterns first would downgrade a genuine vulnerability to 'the service was down' — the single misclassification that would turn a reliability wrapper into a security regression.

audit_governance._note: Any invocation of a listed command in a workflow `run:` block must be routed through the matching approved wrapper. The audit POLICY (threshold, --locked) stays visible at the call site rather than moving inside a wrapper where it could be lowered out of sight.

download_governance._note: Tool downloads inside a required check are an external dependency like any other. Before Phase 1 these were bare `curl -fsSL` with no timeout and no retry, inside a ten-minute job: a GitHub Releases blip reddened the required integrity context, and a SLOW one consumed the budget and cancelled every control after it.
download_governance._m50_note: M50 Phase 1 widened this from a single workflow to every workflow. A probe confirmed a bare `curl https://...` added to security.yml was accepted by every validator, because the rule was scoped to workflow-integrity.yml alone.

non_download_curl_exemptions.reason: Health and readiness probes against the locally-booted compose stack. No artefact is fetched and no third party is involved; the bounded-download wrapper would be meaningless here. The recovery loop that uses them already carries its own 120s deadline.
Same locally-booted health, readiness and smoke probes.
Post-deploy smoke probe against the environment just deployed, already bounded with --max-time 30. Not an artefact download.
Governance evidence query against the GitHub API, already bounded with --max-time 30 --retry 2 --retry-connrefused. Fetches JSON evidence, not an executable artefact, and has no checksum to verify.

npm_network_policy._note: npm's defaults are fetch-retries=2 with fetch-retry-maxtimeout=60000, serialised across many requests. That is how one `npm audit` consumed 7m01s on 2026-09-04. Installation and auditing get different budgets because they are different operations: an install legitimately makes hundreds of requests, an audit makes one.

install.rationale: Retry stays enabled — a dropped request mid-install is common and cheap to retry — but the per-retry ceiling drops from 60s to 20s, bounding the tail without changing behaviour on a healthy registry.

audit.rationale: npm's internal retry is disabled entirely and replaced by the wrapper's own bounded, classified, observable retry. Two retry layers stacked would multiply, not add.

publish.rationale: No workflow publishes an npm package. Recorded so that adding one is a deliberate act that must extend this policy.

composer_network_policy._note: `shivammathur/setup-php` exports COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0 into the runner environment — zero meaning UNLIMITED. Verified verbatim in the `Dependency audit` and `Governance Advisory` job logs on 4f3f62d. A governed audit path must not inherit that.

audit.rationale: The wrapper sets COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT explicitly and additionally imposes its own hard per-attempt timeout, so an unlimited inherited value cannot reach a governed audit.

exit_code_semantics.0: clean — composer audited and found nothing
exit_code_semantics.100: generic composer error — NEVER a verdict; classified UNAVAILABLE

workflow_integrity_budget._note: The required integrity job runs more live external operations than any other job in the repository, and is the only one with a tight cap. Before Phase 1 nobody had multiplied these out; the cancellation on 2026-09-04 was the arithmetic asserting itself. The validator now recomputes this sum from the components below and fails if it exceeds the declared timeout.

fixed_overhead.note: Checkout, two extractions, actionlint over 14 files, and every structural control that makes no network call. Measured healthy total for the whole job was 104s on run 33879626208; 150 carries headroom.

governed_downloads.note: 3 attempts x 15s + (2s + 4s) backoff. actionlint and shellcheck.

live_npm_audits.note: 2 attempts x 25s + 4s backoff. M45 Part B runs two; M47 case C re-executes the entire M45 control, so it runs two more.

live_composer_audits.note: 2 attempts x 15s + 4s backoff. Same doubling as npm.

baseline_git_fetch.note: 2 attempts x 15s + 4s backoff, once per M45 control execution.

workflow_integrity_budget.why_not_a_separate_job: Splitting the live dependency-audit controls into their own job was evaluated and REJECTED. A new job is a new status-check context, and a new context is not in the ruleset, so the live audit controls would silently stop being required — a bypass created by a change made in the name of reliability. Bounding every operation and computing the total achieves the same protection without detaching anything from the required context.

control_manifest._note: A job's conclusion tells you whether it finished, never which of its controls ran. When the integrity job was cancelled on 2026-09-04, four controls produced no result and reconstructing which ones required reading step timings by hand. Each enforced control now writes a completion record, and a final step asserts the recorded set is exactly the mandatory set.

masking_governance._note: M50 Phase 1. Before this, masking was checked in exactly two workflows (security.yml via the audit gate, staging-deploy.yml via deployment safety) and in five reliability scripts. Twelve of fourteen workflows were unchecked, and a probe confirmed that adding `|| true` to a GA certification command was accepted by every validator. The rule is now repository-wide.
masking_governance._why_not_a_blanket_ban: Some `||` constructs are correct and removing them would break working jobs. `grep` exits 1 when it matches nothing, so `grep ... || true` is the idiom for 'collect matches, there may be none'. Teardown must run whether or not the thing being torn down came up. And a reporting step that runs after a gate has already decided cannot change that decision. So the ban is on UNEXPLAINED masking: every exemption below names a workflow, a step and a reason, and a construct that matches none of them fails the check.
masking_governance._no_wildcards: There is deliberately no way to exempt a whole workflow, a whole construct, or a path prefix. An exemption is (workflow, step, construct, reason) or it does not exist. A future maintainer adding a mask must say where and why.

exemptions.reason: Artifact upload after the test gate. Runs so coverage is retrievable from a failed run; cannot change the job's conclusion.
grep no-match idiom: `grep -E 'starting|unhealthy' || true` returns empty when every container is healthy, which is the success case.
`docker compose down -v` after the gate. Must run on failure or the runner leaks volumes; cannot change the conclusion.
Pre-flight teardown of a stack that may not exist yet. Failure here means there was nothing to remove, which is the desired starting state.
grep no-match idiom, as in ci-docker.yml.
Diagnostic log collection on an already-failing run. A container that died may have no logs to collect; failing here would replace the real error with a log-collection error.

exemptions.step: Clean teardown (remove volumes — no state persists)
exemptions.reason: Teardown after the gate, as in ci-docker.yml.

M33, and load-bearing. A bare `needs:` SKIPS the aggregator when a dependency fails, and GitHub treats a skipped required check as pending rather than failed. `always()` makes it run; the job then compares needs.android.result and needs.ios.result against the literal 'success' and fails on anything else. Removing this would reopen the M29-A pending trap.
Reporting step after the ratchet has already decided. Built from JSON the ratchet wrote; scrapes no console text and cannot alter the conclusion.
Evidence artifact upload after the gate.
Summary rendered from the k6 summary JSON after the run. Guarded by `if [ -f ... ]`; reports, gates nothing.
k6 result artifact upload after the run.
Soak-profile result artifact upload after the run. The step is unnamed in the workflow; matched by its position as the upload-artifact step of the soak job.

deferred_defects.step: Migrate from an empty database + seed bootstrap
deferred_defects.blocked_by: Bare `php artisan db:seed --force` resolves Database\Seeders\DatabaseSeeder, then bare DatabaseSeeder; this repository deliberately provides neither, so the command fails with BindingResolutionException before any SQL — verified against a fully migrated 132-table database. Unmasking makes both Docker gates fail deterministically on every run. Seeding here is module-scoped (11 module seeders, 9 verified working); the architecture is valid and the INVOCATION is wrong.
deferred_defects.why_not_fixed_here: The correct fix is an application-level root DatabaseSeeder contract under apps/api/database/seeders/, outside M50 Phase 1's authorised .github/** boundary. The .github/**-only alternative — replacing the bare command with an explicit --class list — was considered and REJECTED by owner decision: it encodes the product seeding contract in a workflow file, duplicates the seeder list across two workflows with no validator keeping them in sync, and could not be proven against PostgreSQL/Redis because the Docker daemon was unavailable during analysis. Deleting the command was also rejected: the seeding intent is real.
deferred_defects.remedy: Owner-approved deferral. Out-of-scope milestone owning apps/** must: (a) add apps/api/database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php calling the 10 resolvable module seeders, excluding MarketplaceSeeder; (b) bind or refactor MarketplaceSeeder's `string $currency` before including it; (c) validate the whole seed in the real Docker certification path against PostgreSQL and Redis, confirming NigerianFoodSeeder's Search/Redis indexing path succeeds; (d) only then remove these two masks.
deferred_defects.classification: BLOCKED - ROOT CAUSE REQUIRES OUT-OF-SCOPE CHANGE
corrected_finding: 1. The modular seeding architecture is VALID. Seeding is module-scoped by design, exactly as migrations are: 19 module service providers each call loadMigrationsFrom(). There is no seeder-discovery mechanism and none is intended.

2. 11 module seeders exist, under modules/<Module>/src/Infrastructure/Seeder/: Admin, Ai (DefaultPromptSeeder), Catalog (NigerianFoodSeeder), Commerce, Loyalty, Marketplace, Notifications, Nutrition (NutritionItemSeeder), Payments, Reviews, Support.

3. 9 of those 11 succeeded (exit 0) when invoked individually with --class= against an isolated, fully migrated SQLite database (132 tables), each run starting from a fresh copy: Admin, Ai, Commerce, Loyalty, Notifications, Nutrition, Payments, Reviews, Support.

4. MarketplaceSeeder has an INDEPENDENT defect unrelated to this finding: its constructor takes a required primitive `string $currency` which the container cannot autowire and for which no binding exists anywhere in the application. It fails with 'Unresolvable dependency resolving [Parameter #3 [ <required> string $currency ]]' in every environment, and is therefore EXCLUDED from the proposed aggregator until that dependency is bound.

5. NigerianFoodSeeder failed only on this analysis host, with RedisException: Connection refused, raised from modules/Search/src/Infrastructure/Event/DomainEventSubscriber.php:34 via EventIndexTranslator.php:79 — the Search module indexes the domain events the seeder emits. Both Docker workflows boot and health-gate Redis, so it is expected to pass there, but that is NOT PROVEN: the Docker daemon was unavailable during analysis. It MUST be validated in the actual Docker environment before any unmasking.
6. Both workflows currently invoke bare `php artisan db:seed --force`, with no --class argument.

7. Laravel's SeedCommand::getSeeder() resolves the root seeder Database\Seeders\DatabaseSeeder and then falls back to a bare DatabaseSeeder. This repository deliberately provides NEITHER: apps/api/database/seeders/ contains only .gitkeep, composer.json PSR-4 maps Database\Seeders\ to that empty directory, and no DatabaseSeeder class exists anywhere outside vendor/.

8. The command therefore fails DETERMINISTICALLY, before any SQL: BindingResolutionException 'Target class [DatabaseSeeder] does not exist'. Verified against a fully migrated 132-table database — migration state, step ordering, and database initialisation are all correct and change nothing. Resolution fails inside Model::unguarded() before the connection is touched.

9. The existing `|| true` / `|| echo` masking hides that deterministic failure. git log -S 'db:seed' shows exactly one commit per workflow (eeca65d M20-part-3 for ci-docker.yml, bbb32b1 M22 for ga-docker-certification.yml); both introduced the command ALREADY MASKED. It has never run unmasked and has never once succeeded.

10. The safe remediation is application-level: establish a real root DatabaseSeeder contract at apps/api/database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php that calls the 10 resolvable module seeders (all except MarketplaceSeeder), followed by validation in the actual Docker certification path against PostgreSQL and Redis, and only then removal of the masks.

11. That remediation is OUTSIDE M50 Phase 1, whose authorised file boundary is .github/** only. Phase 1 must not create it, must not modify apps/**, and must not encode the product seeding contract into a workflow as an explicit --class list.

root_cause_analysis.workflow_ordering_or_configuration: RULED OUT. Both workflows order boot -> health-gate -> migrate --force -> db:seed correctly.
root_cause_analysis.incomplete_module_migration_discovery: RULED OUT. 19 loadMigrationsFrom() calls; a full migrate produces 132 tables; catalog_categories is created by Catalog migration 2026_02_01_000001_create_catalog_categories_table.php.
root_cause_analysis.application_or_module_registration: PARTIAL, secondary only. MarketplaceSeeder is not container-resolvable; this does not cause the bare db:seed failure.
root_cause_analysis.environment_or_database_initialisation: RULED OUT. Migration succeeds and 9 seeders write successfully against the migrated database.
root_cause_analysis.actual_cause: The workflows invoke Laravel's default ROOT-SEEDER ENTRY POINT in a repository that deliberately provides no root seeder.

concurrency_governance._note: M50 Phase 1. ci-docker.yml was the only workflow of fourteen with no concurrency group, so a superseded run kept building images and booting a compose stack nobody was waiting for. Every workflow's concurrency behaviour is now stated here, so the next one to go missing is a policy violation rather than something nobody notices.

cancel_in_progress_exemptions.reason: Tag-triggered production release. Cancelling a half-finished release run would leave images built and a release gate un-evaluated; two tags are independent releases and must both complete.
Deploys to a live staging environment. Cancelling mid-rollout leaves the cluster in a partially-updated state; the single `staging-deploy` group serialises deployments instead.
Long-running k6 scenarios including a 2h soak. A superseding run must not discard hours of in-flight measurement.

network_policies._note: M50 Phase 1. npm was the only ecosystem with a network policy; composer, flutter and apt had none, and setup-php exports COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0 (unlimited) into every job. Each entry names how the bound is expressed, because the mechanisms genuinely differ: composer has an env var, apt has command options, and pub has neither — so its bound is a step timeout.

composer_install.rationale: setup-php exports COMPOSER_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=0 — zero meaning UNLIMITED, verified verbatim in the Dependency audit and Governance Advisory job logs. 300s is generous for a cached install and finite for a stalled one.

flutter_pub_get.rationale: Dart's pub exposes no network-timeout or retry environment variable, so an env-based bound would be theatre. The honest bound is a step-level timeout: native to Actions, explicit, and verifiable.

apt_get_install.rationale: apt has native retry and timeout options. Note the detector is a regex, not a substring: once the options are inserted, `apt-get install` is no longer contiguous text.

network_policies._docker_deferred: Docker registry pull/push bounds and the production Dockerfiles' own retry logic are M50 Phase 2. Phase 1 is forbidden to modify infra/**.
